utilities.name: arrayMove
utilities.description:
Move an item to another index, returning a new array (the input is not mutated).

Negative indices count from the end. If `from` is out of range, an unchanged copy is returned.

signatures.text: arrayMove<T>(array: T[], from: number, to: number): T[]

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Index of the item to move (negative counts from the end)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Index to move the item to (negative counts from the end)

returns.description: A new array with the item moved

utilities.name: publish
utilities.description:
Run `pnpm changeset publish`, authenticating with the `NPM_TOKEN` from `.env.local`
through a temporary `.npmrc` that is deleted afterwards.

Exits the process with code 1 when `NPM_TOKEN` is missing. Also available as the
`changeset-publish` CLI (`--dry-run`, `--next`).

signatures.text: publish(options: { isDryRun: boolean; isNext: boolean }): void

properties.name: isDryRun
properties.description: Pass `--dry-run` to `changeset publish`

properties.name: isNext
properties.description: Publish under the `next` dist-tag

examples: publish({ isDryRun: true, isNext: false });

utilities.name: getHighestZindex
utilities.description:
Find the highest computed `z-index` among all descendants of an element.

Descendants with `z-index: auto` and `<script>` elements are ignored.

signatures.text: getHighestZindex(element?: HTMLElement | Document, defaultZindex: number = 0): number

parameters.name: defaultZindex
parameters.description: Value returned when no descendant has a numeric z-index (default: 0)

returns.description: The highest z-index found, or `defaultZindex`

examples:
// Place a new overlay above everything on the page
overlay.style.zIndex = String(getHighestZindex() + 1);

utilities.name: getParents
utilities.description: Collect the ancestors of an element, nearest first, up to and including `document.body`.

signatures.text: getParents(elm: HTMLElement | Element, options?: { breakBefore?: (element: HTMLElement | Element) => boolean; breakAfter?: (element: HTMLElement | Element) => boolean }): HTMLElement[]

parameters.name: elm
parameters.description: The element whose ancestors to collect

parameters.name: options
parameters.type: { breakBefore?: (element: HTMLElement | Element) => boolean; breakAfter?: (element: HTMLElement | Element) => boolean }

properties.name: breakBefore
properties.description: Stop before adding the first ancestor that matches

properties.name: breakAfter
properties.description: Stop after adding the first ancestor that matches

returns.description: The ancestor elements, from the direct parent outwards

examples:
getParents(button); // [form, section, main, body]
getParents(button, { breakAfter: (el) => el.matches('form') }); // [form]

utilities.name: sumOfParentZindex
utilities.description:
Sum the inline `style.zIndex` of every ancestor of an element (see `getParents`).

Only inline styles are read, not stylesheet or computed values. Ancestors without
a numeric inline z-index count as `parentDefaultZindex`.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: The element whose ancestors to sum

parameters.name: parentDefaultZindex
parameters.description: Value used for ancestors without a numeric inline z-index (default: 0)

returns.description: The summed z-index of all ancestors

examples:
//
sumOfParentZindex(document.querySelector('#target')!); // 15

utilities.name: isDevelopment

Detect development mode at runtime from `DEV`/`NODE_ENV` in `process.env` or

utilities.deprecated:
⚠️ WARNING: This function PREVENTS dead code elimination in production builds!

Bundlers cannot optimize away calls to this function because:
1. It's a function call (not a constant)
2. Runtime typeof checks prevent compile-time evaluation

❌ DON'T USE THIS: if (isDevelopment()) { devOnlyCode(); }
✅ USE THIS INSTEAD: if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') { devOnlyCode(); }

The direct check allows bundlers to eliminate dead code at build time.
Only use this function if you need runtime environment detection.

utilities.name: loadEnvFiles
utilities.description:
Loads environment variables from .env files into `process.env`.
Earlier files in the list take precedence over later ones, and variables that
are already set are never overridden.

signatures.text: loadEnvFiles(options?: { keys?: string[]; files?: string[]; cwd?: string }): void

parameters.name: options
parameters.type: { keys?: string[]; files?: string[]; cwd?: string }

properties.name: keys
properties.description: Array of specific keys to load (loads all if not specified)

properties.name: files
properties.description: Array of file paths to load (defaults to ['.env.local', '.env', '.env.secret'])

properties.name: cwd
properties.description: Directory the files are resolved against (defaults to process.cwd())

examples:
loadEnvFiles(); // .env.local, .env and .env.secret from process.cwd()
loadEnvFiles({ files: ['.env.test'], keys: ['DATABASE_URL'] });

utilities.name: loadRootEnvFiles
utilities.description:
Loads env files from the repository root so every app in a monorepo shares
one set of values.

Never overrides: variables already set (by the shell, CI, or an app's own
`.env*` loading) win, and earlier files in `files` win over later ones.

properties.name: files
properties.description: Env files to load from the repository root, highest precedence first.

properties.name: from
properties.description:
Where to start searching for the repository root: a file or directory path,
or a file URL such as `import.meta.url`. Defaults to `process.cwd()`.

properties.name: rootMarkers
properties.description: Files or directories whose presence marks the repository root.

returns.description: The repository root, or `undefined` if none was found (nothing is loaded).

examples:
// apps/web/next.config.ts
loadRootEnvFiles({ from: import.meta.url });

utilities.name: findRoot
utilities.description:
Walks up the directory tree from `start` and returns the first directory
that satisfies `check`. Errors thrown by `check` are treated as a non-match.

signatures.text: findRoot(start: string = process.cwd(), check: FindRootCheck = hasPackageJson): string

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Directory (or file path) to start from. Defaults to `process.cwd()`.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: Predicate run on each directory. Defaults to "contains a package.json".

returns.description: The absolute path of the first matching directory.

examples:
findRoot(); // nearest directory with a package.json, from process.cwd()
findRoot(import.meta.dirname, (dir) => existsSync(join(dir, 'pnpm-workspace.yaml')));

utilities.name: FindRootCheck
utilities.description: TypeScript type exported by @pixpilot/fs.

utilities.name: isGuidString
utilities.description:
Check if a string matches the canonical GUID format.

This implementation is optimized for repeated checks by validating fixed
positions before scanning the remaining hexadecimal characters.

returns.description: True if the string matches `8-4-4-4-12` hex characters, false otherwise

examples:

utilities.name: simpleHash
utilities.description:
Compute a fast, non-cryptographic 32-bit hash of a string.

⚠️ WARNING: Not cryptographically secure. Use only for cache keys, bucketing,
and other non-sensitive identifiers. For security, use `crypto.subtle.digest()` or bcrypt.

signatures.text: simpleHash(str: string, radix: number = DEFAULT_RADIX): string

parameters.name: radix
parameters.description: Base of the returned string, 2 to 36 (default: 36)

returns.description: The absolute hash value as a string in the given radix

examples:
simpleHash('hello'); // '1n1e4y'
simpleHash('hello', 16); // '5e918d2'

utilities.name: ToSnakeCase
utilities.description:
Convert camelCase to snake_case at the type level.

This intentionally matches the runtime behavior of `change-case`'s `snakeCase`
for camelCase conversion: inserts underscores before uppercase letters and lowercases.
utilities.type: type ToSnakeCase<S extends string> = S extends `${infer P1}${infer P2}${infer P3}` ? P1 extends Lowercase<P1> ? P2 extends Uppercase<P2> ? `${P1}_${ToSnakeCase<`${Lowercase<P2>}${P3}`>}` : `${P1}${ToSnakeCase<`${P2}${P3}`>}` : S : S;
